records.title: [Perf] Consume linear NVFP4 scales in FlashInfer CUTLASS A2A MoE
records.body:
## Motivation

Consume FlashInfer A2A's linear NVFP4 scales directly in CUTLASS input expansion, removing the intermediate interleave using [FlashInfer #2330](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2330) ([#2200](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2200)).

## Modifications

- Pass `swizzled_input_sf=False` for `H % 64 == 0`; validate layout and retain the unaligned fallback.
- Delegate Standard prefill/extend inputs to the existing wrapper.

## Accuracy Tests

Passed on **1×B200**: linear-scale and unaligned fallback parity against explicit interleave (`H=128/288`, `rtol=atol=1e-3`), output buffer reuse, and Standard dispatch parity (output type and numerics).

```bash
python3 test/registered/kernel/moe/test_flashinfer_cutlass_nvfp4_scales.py -v
```

Tested on **4×B200**, TP=EP=DP=4, with `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, FlashInfer 0.6.18 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. GSM8K: 200 questions, 5-shot, 128 threads, temperature 0, max 512 output tokens.

<details>
<summary>Server and evaluation commands</summary>

```bash
SGLANG_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH=1 \
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION=0 \
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096 \
sglang serve --model-path nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --revision 2538ded2a4edb247b4d2b4a8ba24e44bd4c017c3 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --dp 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer \
  --max-prefill-tokens 4096 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --disable-radix-cache --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --random-seed 42 --watchdog-timeout 300 --port 30000
```

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --model nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 --eval-name gsm8k --api completion \
  --num-examples 200 --num-threads 128 --max-tokens 512 \
  --num-shots 5 --temperature 0
```

</details>

| Configuration | GSM8K run 1 | GSM8K run 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Swizzled control | 90.5% | 92.5% |
| This PR (linear) | 91.5% | 91.5% |

Control uses the same implementation with `swizzled_input_sf=True`. The runs are independent; an earlier 64-thread paired evaluation scored 92.5% versus 91.5%, so accuracy equivalence remains unverified.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Profiling on 4×B200 with Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4: across 20 matched rank/step pairs (4 ranks × 5 CUDA Graph decode steps, batch size 8 per rank), interleave launches decrease from 48 to 0 per rank and step, with unchanged copy counts and no added in-step synchronization/allocation.
- Serving on 4×B200 with the same model, TP=EP=DP=4: 128 requests, max concurrency 64, input/output lengths sampled from 1–1024/1–128 tokens. Mean TPOT (control → linear) is 53.36 → 46.69 ms and 51.92 → 44.14 ms in two paired runs. Separate control runs reach 41.51–46.81 ms, so a stable serving speedup remains unverified.

Historical full synthetic `dispatch → MoE → combine`: **H=2048, I=1024, E=32, K=2**, BF16 output, balanced `R` tokens/source, TP=EP=DP. Both variants use B200 GPUs, FlashInfer 0.6.18, torch 2.13.0+cu130 and CUDA 13.0. Baseline includes interleave; linear consumes scales directly. Correctness gates exercise the production wrapper; timing uses the shared CUTLASS helper and real communication.

| EP | Tokens/source | Run 02: baseline → linear (µs) | Run 03: baseline → linear (µs) | Paired latency reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 2048 | 146.898 → 139.771 | 140.770 → 134.910 | 3.749%–4.233% |
| 4 | 4096 | 226.051 → 218.708 | 222.081 → 214.454 | 3.636%–4.412% |
| 4 | 8192 | 386.008 → 373.136 | 382.333 → 368.862 | 3.522%–3.526% |
| 8 | 2048 | 152.819 → 146.606 | 151.825 → 142.594 | 5.567%–7.174% |
| 8 | 4096 | 236.530 → 225.151 | 240.221 → 226.164 | 5.388%–6.061% |
| 8 | 8192 | 416.683 → 390.500 | 412.721 → 390.890 | 5.589%–6.261% |

Warm-cache CUDA Graph timing: 20 warmups, 10 alternating AB/BA rounds, 20 replays/sample, 10 chains/Graph; PDL and fused finalize enabled, online autotuning disabled, A/A controls at R=64/8192. Latencies are medians of per-round maximum-rank times. Reductions are medians of paired per-round percentages; ranges span two independent runs, not confidence intervals, and need not match ratios of displayed medians.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no user-facing API or configuration changes.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

records.title: [MoonEP] Use DeepGEMM psum layout, zero-copy shard and other optimization
records.body:
This PR adds several optimization to improve MoonEP+DeepGEMM performance for Kimi K3:
1. Use DeepGEMM psum layout
2. Zero-copy dispatch/combine
3. Padding tokens no longer route to expert 0

## Result

Steady-state decode, greedy, 128 output tokens, `decode_bench.py`:

| concurrency | before (tok/s) | after (tok/s) | after + DSPARK γ=7 (tok/s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (per request) | 6.06 | 15.9 (2.6x) | 37.6 (6.2x) |
| 8 (aggregate) | 48.5 | 128.5 (2.65x) | 239 (4.9x) |
| 32 (aggregate) | 190 | 458 (2.4x) | 663 (3.5x) |

Decode step at c=8: 165 ms -> 62 ms. One MoE layer: 1.69 ms -> 0.62 ms.
gsm8k (200 questions, greedy): 0.995 before, 0.990 after, 0.995 with DSPARK.

records.title: [ROCm] Route per-head QK norm to the stride-aware JIT kernel instead of copying
records.body:
## Motivation

`apply_qk_norm`'s fused fast path is gated on `_is_cuda`, with a `TODO(dark)` saying it has not been tried elsewhere. On ROCm it therefore falls through to `_reshape_for_qk_norm`, i.e. `x.reshape(-1, head_dim)`. `q`/`k` are last-dim slices of the fused QKV projection, so their rows are strided over the K/V columns and that flatten is not expressible with the input's strides — `reshape` silently degrades to `.contiguous()`, a whole-tensor device copy every layer, every forward. It is paid whether or not AITER is enabled, because the flatten lives in the model layer rather than a kernel wrapper.

Qwen3-8B on 1xMI325X (gfx942):

```
q (T, 32, 128) stride=(6144, 128, 1) bf16   reshape(-1,128) shares storage: False
k (T,  8, 128) stride=(6144, 128, 1) bf16   reshape(-1,128) shares storage: False
```

`6144 = 32*128 + 8*128 + 8*128` is the fused-QKV row stride, which pins the mechanism exactly.

The kernel behind the gate already accepts that layout — `qknorm.cuh` takes `q_stride`/`k_stride` and indexes `token * stride + head * head_dim` — and the JIT toolchain already targets HIP. Enabling it gives **+2.02% on Qwen3-8B and +3.11% on Qwen3-30B-A3B end to end, 3.4x at the kernel level**.

## Modifications

- `qknorm.cuh`: wrap two redundant unguarded `cuda_bf16.h` / `cuda_fp16.h` includes in `#ifndef USE_ROCM`. `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`, included four lines above, already maps them to `hip/hip_*.h` and defines an empty `__grid_constant__`. These two lines were the only thing blocking the ROCm build (`fatal error: 'cuda_bf16.h' file not found`).
- `models/utils.py`: widen the gate from `_is_cuda` to `(_is_cuda or _is_hip)`. The other five conditions are platform-independent and left as they are; `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` still degrades to the old path when the kernel cannot be built for a given `head_dim`/dtype (supported: 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024).
- New `test/registered/kernel/jit/test_qknorm_strided.py`, registered for AMD CI.

**Not #21734 again.** That was reverted by #23159 because a stride-preserving 3-D view was handed to **AITER**, whose RMSNorm kernels fault on strided input. Here the strided view goes only to the JIT kernel, which carries the strides in its signature; the AITER fallback still receives the flattened 2-D tensor.

**Scope.** The 13 models on the shared `apply_qk_norm`: `qwen3`, `qwen3_moe`, `glm4_moe`, `llama4`, `bailing_moe`, `dflash`, `laguna`, `llada2`, `mellum`, `muse_glimmer`, `sdar`, `sdar_moe`, `inkling`. Models with a *local* `_apply_qk_norm` are not reached, and they split into two groups:

- **The Qwen3.5 stack already has a stride-aware path and pays no copy.** `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer` defaults to `attn_output_gate=True`, so on HIP/XPU/CPU it takes `forward_prepare_fused_gate` → `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate`, whose kernel already does two-level `token * stride + head * stride` indexing and whose wrapper uses `view()`, not `reshape()`. This covers Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6-397B, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (ships as `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next / Qwen4-Exp (`Qwen4ExpAttentionDecoderLayer` inherits it and hard-sets the gate). A dispatch probe on Qwen3.5-122B confirms it: 361 calls, all to the gated kernel, none to the shared helper.
- **Still copying, and genuine follow-ups:** `qwen3_next`, `afmoe`, `lfm2`, and `bailing_moe_linear` / `bailing_moe_v3` when `use_qk_norm` is on — these inline `reshape(-1, head_dim)` in the model file.

`olmo2` looks like a candidate but normalizes the full hidden width, not per head. **NVIDIA is unaffected by construction** — see the first comment below.

One latent issue this PR does *not* fix: the non-gated `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm` still does `q.reshape(-1, head_dim)` and then passes `q_flat.stride(0)` to a kernel that declares a row-stride parameter — a value that can only ever be `head_dim`, so the parameter is dead and the docstring's "without an extra `.contiguous()` copy" does not hold. No shipped Qwen3.5-family config reaches it (they all gate), so it is latent rather than costly today.

## Accuracy Tests

New test: **30/30 on MI325X**, over 5 geometries (GQA 4:1 / 2:1, MHA, `head_dim` 64/128/256) x {bf16, fp16}. It asserts strided vs dense output is **bit-identical** (`torch.equal`), matches an fp32 per-head reference at `atol=rtol=2e-2`, preserves `data_ptr`, leaves the V columns of the shared buffer untouched (sentinel), and stays finite with V poisoned to NaN. The existing `test_qknorm.py` only ever builds standalone contiguous `q`/`k`, so nothing in tree had fed this kernel a strided fused-QKV slice.

GSM8K, 500 questions, 5-shot, greedy, Qwen3-8B, base vs patched at the same commit: **0.920 vs 0.920**, 0 invalid on both.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Kernel level.** Per-call GPU time from replaying a captured graph of 20 calls over 4 rotating QKV buffers (timing the Python callable is dispatch-bound at ~30 us/call and hides the kernel), best of 3 x 50 replays, bf16, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. `cur/slice` is today's ROCm path; `cur/dense` holds that provider fixed and only densifies the input so `reshape` becomes a free view, which isolates the copy.

| geometry | tokens | cur/slice | cur/dense | fused | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B 32q/8kv | 4096 | 123.4 us | 98.7 us | 39.0 us | 3.16x |
| Qwen3-8B 32q/8kv | 8192 | 234.8 us | 191.1 us | 56.1 us | 4.18x |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B 32q/4kv | 8192 | 211.8 us | 172.7 us | 60.1 us | 3.52x |
| **sum, 12 cases** | | **1184.7 us** | **938.9 us** | **349.7 us** | **3.39x** |

Median 3.21x. Of the 835.0 us saved, **245.8 us (29%) is the copy** and 589.1 us (71%) is AITER's two norm launches trailing the single fused kernel. The same 29/71 split was measured independently for the equivalent vLLM path on gfx942, which is a useful cross-check on both.

**End to end.** `sglang.benchmark.offline_throughput`, random 1024-in / 128-out, `--disable-radix-cache`, TP=1, 1xMI325X. Three interleaved base/patched pairs per model with the order alternated per repeat, so drift and thermal ramp are shared rather than charged to one arm; deltas are pairwise and the figure is the median. Both arms are the same tree at the same commit differing only in the gate, so weights, JIT cache and aiter build are shared.

| Model | pairwise | median | within-arm spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | +2.02 / +1.99 / +3.20 % | **+2.02 %** | base 1.21 %, patch 0.92 % |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | +2.73 / +3.40 / +3.11 % | **+3.11 %** | base 1.21 %, patch 1.85 % |
| Qwen3-0.6B | +4.46 / −0.08 / +3.83 % | +3.83 % | base 1.73 %, patch 3.74 % |
| Mistral-7B (control) | −0.21 / +1.23 / −0.38 % | **−0.21 %** | base 1.26 %, patch 1.51 % |

Mistral-7B has no `q_norm`/`k_norm`, never reaches the helper, and comes out flat within its own spread. Qwen3-0.6B is **not** load-bearing: one of its three pairs is negative and its patched spread exceeds its median delta, because at that size the run is scheduler-bound. Reported rather than dropped.

Tested on gfx942 (MI325X) only; gfx950 (MI355X) numbers to follow.

<details>
<summary>Dispatch coverage — which models actually change, measured not assumed</summary>

Instrumented both `fused_inplace_qknorm` and `_reshape_for_qk_norm` to record every distinct `(shape, stride, dtype, verdict)`, then ran one short generate per model on both trees. These are dispatch counts, so they do not depend on clean timing.

| Model | layout reaching `apply_qk_norm` | calls whose 2-D flatten would copy |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | q `(T,32,128)` / k `(T,8,128)`, stride 6144 | **11018 / 11234** |
| Qwen3-0.6B | q `(T,16,128)` / k `(T,8,128)`, stride 4096 | **8570 / 8738** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | q `(T,32,128)` / k `(T,4,128)`, stride 5120 | **14690 / 14978** |
| lfm2-1.2b | never reaches it (local `_apply_qk_norm`) | — |
| Mistral-7B | never reaches it (no QK norm) | — |
| Olmo-3-7B | never reaches it (full-width norm) | — |

On base, the identical 11018/11234 calls go through `_reshape_for_qk_norm` and copy, so the correspondence is one-to-one. The residual 216 calls are the `T == 1` decode graphs, where the leading dim is degenerate and the flatten is already free — worth stating plainly: this is a prefill and multi-sequence-decode cost, not a universal per-forward cost.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Why the other five gate conditions are kept as-is</summary>

I read them one at a time rather than assuming they were all CUDA-specific:

| condition | why it is kept |
|---|---|
| `allow_inplace` | caller semantics, platform-independent |
| `q_eps == k_eps` | the kernel takes a single `eps` |
| `not SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_INFERENCE` | platform-independent |
| `tc_compiler != "inductor"` | `tc_compiler` is a platform-agnostic knob defaulting to `"eager"`; when inductor PCG *is* on, letting it fuse the norm is the same call as on CUDA |
| `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm(head_dim, q.dtype)` | the real capability check — `@cache_once`, catches build failures and returns `False` |

One pre-existing property, now more exposed: the kernel's `TensorMatcher` requires the norm weight dtype to equal the activation dtype, and `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm` does not check the weight. A model arriving with an fp32 norm weight would fail the matcher — but the set of models calling `apply_qk_norm` is platform-independent and the gate is already open on CUDA, so this PR cannot introduce a new instance of it. The dispatch probe shows `w_dtype=bfloat16` for all three models measured.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation — N/A, no user-facing surface and no new flags.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

records.title: [MegaMoE] Preserve W13 layout for ModelOpt NVFP4 experts
records.body:
Depends on #38080.

This PR is stacked directly on the current #38080 head (`2f9270f891`). Until #38080 merges, GitHub may show the parent PR's changes as part of this PR. The additional commits to review are `f6d2ef53f9` (two production files, 17 insertions and 2 deletions), `71697cb8ba` (one focused CPU regression-test file), and `79456378e0` (Ruff formatting only).

## Motivation

DeepSeek V4 ModelOpt NVFP4 can retain `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` as its nominal MoE runner while `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` bypasses that runner and sends the expert weights to DeepGEMM MegaMoE.

The loader previously selected W31 from the nominal runner. MegaMoE consumes canonical W13 and interprets the first half as gate and the second half as up. The mismatch therefore swaps the SwiGLU nonlinear operands and causes a large accuracy loss. The same mismatch can be reproduced by explicitly pairing a TRT-LLM nominal runner with MegaMoE on Qwen NVFP4.

## Modifications

- Add a ModelOpt-NVFP4-specific `use_flashinfer_trtllm_weight_layout` decision. It selects W31 only when the effective consumer is TRT-LLM; MegaMoE always selects canonical W13.
- Use that decision for the W1/W3 shard mapping and for optional interleaved W13 deinterleaving.
- Assert the canonical-W13 invariant before building MegaMoE NVFP4 weights.
- Keep the existing layer-level runner flag unchanged. FP8, MxInt4, unquantized/BF16, padding, runner selection, and existing guards retain their previous behavior.
- Add a registered CPU unit suite covering the backend/layout matrix, real shard placement for weights and scales, unchanged non-ModelOpt loading, interleaved post-load handling, the invariant guard, and the online ModelOpt subclass.

The DeepSeek V4 fix is the loader shard mapping. The deinterleave change keeps the Inkling-style interleaved loader consistent with the same contract; that path is covered by focused unit tests but was not part of the DeepSeek GPU evaluation.

## Accuracy Tests

All reported full GSM8K runs evaluated 1,314/1,314 examples and completed without an inference-time product error.

| Model/path | GB300 | B300 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, normal MegaMoE (`runner=auto`) | 93.46% | 94.90% |
| Qwen NVFP4, forced nominal TRT-routed / actual MegaMoE | 92.47% | 93.00% |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro NVFP4, aggregate DSpark, target/draft MegaMoE | 94.98% | 94.52% |

Additional DeepSeek-V4-Pro NVFP4 full runs on GB300:

- aggregate MegaMoE without DSpark: 95.28%;
- disaggregated MegaMoE without DSpark: 96.96%;
- disaggregated DSpark target/draft MegaMoE, DEP8: 97.34%;
- disaggregated DSpark target/draft MegaMoE, DEP16: 97.34%.

Focused unchanged-path controls also passed: true TRT-LLM/W31 (98.0%, 200 examples), FlashInfer MegaMoE (98.0%, 200 examples), and DeepSeek V4 MXFP4 with DSpark MegaMoE/MegaMoE (97.5%, 200 examples).

The original bug was independently reproduced without this fix: DeepSeek V4 NVFP4 MegaMoE scored 25--26% on the same 200-example evaluation, and forced nominal-TRT/actual-MegaMoE Qwen scored 3.5%. With this fix, the corresponding 200-example DeepSeek runs score 98.0--98.5%, and both full Qwen runs above pass on both GPU architectures.

Focused CPU validation:

- exact reviewed source: 7/7 focused tests passed;
- adjacent suite: 27 tests plus 32 parametrized subtests passed;
- `compileall`, `git diff --check`, Black, and isort passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change only affects weight-layout selection during model loading and adds no inference hot-path branch.

Matched B300 fixed-shape checks used two repetitions of 1,024 requests, ISL/OSL 1024/256, and concurrency 64. Relative to the previously validated W13 implementation, final throughput deltas were -0.39% and +0.45%; median TPOT was 0.28% lower in both repetitions. GB300 repetitions also showed no regression. These results are treated as performance parity, not as a speedup claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed code according to the SGLang style checks.
- [x] Add focused unit coverage for the layout decision and unchanged quantization paths.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required; source comments document the weight-layout contract.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed validation results above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

records.title: [HiCache] Add staged write-back for the page-unified KV cache layout
records.body:
## Motivation

Add staged write-back support for the `page_unified` KV cache layout, building on the unified storage layout discussed in #33651 and the GPU staging approach introduced in #21631.

The destination layouts are:

- **MHA:** `(page, head_group, layer, 2, page_size, head_in_group, dim)`, where K=0 and V=1.
- **MLA:** `(page, layer, page_size, dim)`, storing one compressed KV tensor per layer.

## Changes

- Add `hicache_page_unified_relayout_kernel` to gather per-layer GPU KV data into contiguous staging pages using 16-byte vectorized loads and stores.
- Support MHA and MLA through compile-time specialization. MLA has no head-group, separate K/V, or head axes.
- Reuse the existing whole-page D2H copy helpers after GPU relayout.
- Support transfers larger than the caller-provided staging buffer by processing chunks on the current CUDA stream.
- Add MHA and MLA Python entry points and correctness tests in existing files.

This PR implements the write-back primitives and tests. Host-pool integration and load-back support are outside its scope.

## Correctness

**160 test cases passed on NVIDIA H20 after merging `sgl/main`: 80 MHA and 80 MLA cases.**

Tests compare the complete host output against an independently constructed CPU reference using exact equality, including untouched destination pages.

Coverage includes:

- Different head-group counts, layer counts, page sizes, and dimensions.
- MLA compressed KV dimensions of 512 and 576.
- BF16, FP16, and uint8 data.
- int32 and int64 source page indices.
- Reordered pages and repeated source pages.
- Empty transfers, staging reuse, and partial final chunks.
- Execution on a non-default CUDA stream.
- Invalid shapes, alignment, staging capacities, and destination indices.

Ruff, clang-format, and diff whitespace checks passed for the implementation changes.

## Performance

The MHA write-back path was benchmarked on one NVIDIA H20 with PCIe Gen5 ×16, PyTorch 2.9.1 / CUDA 12.8, and CPU/memory bound to the GPU's NUMA node.

Configuration:

- BF16
- 61 layers
- 8 KV heads
- Head dimension: 128
- Page size: 64
- 5 warmup iterations and 25 measured iterations
- Median CUDA-event latency

Bandwidth includes **GPU relayout + D2H transfer**. GB/s counts the KV payload once.

| Tokens | Payload | 1 head group | 2 head groups | 4 head groups | 8 head groups |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 122 MiB | 52.32 GB/s | 52.34 GB/s | 52.33 GB/s | 52.33 GB/s |
| 2048 | 488 MiB | 52.53 GB/s | 52.52 GB/s | 52.53 GB/s | 52.52 GB/s |
| 8192 | 1952 MiB | 52.74 GB/s | 52.74 GB/s | 52.74 GB/s | 52.74 GB/s |

The measured contiguous D2H baseline was **55.0–55.2 GB/s**, so staged write-back reached approximately **95%** of that baseline.

Using a 32-page staging buffer for the 8192-token transfer sustained approximately **52.6 GB/s**.

For 2048 tokens, profiling showed approximately **0.34 ms for GPU relayout** and **9.39 ms for D2H**, indicating that PCIe transfer dominated total latency.

These performance measurements were collected before the MLA extension and the subsequent merge of `sgl/main`. MLA correctness was validated; MLA bandwidth has not been measured.

## Modifications

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

records.title: Add optional strip layout for Inkling speculative convolutions
records.body:
## Why is this change needed?

Add an opt-in strip layout for Inkling speculative short-convolution intermediates: `--enable-inkling-sconv-strip-layout`. It requires CUDA and a linear draft chain; the default remains off.

For convolution width 4, 8 draft tokens and 128 BF16 channels, dense scratch is `[8, 3, 128]` (6,144 bytes); strip scratch is `[8, 128]` (2,048 bytes). Each fresh input is stored once. Accepted state is reconstructed from the existing history and those inputs: old `[10, 20, 30]`, new `[40, 50, 60]`, accepting two gives `[30, 40, 50]`.

Wire the layout through regular and unified pools, memory reservation, the generic writer, both fused Inkling writers, and acceptance commit. Tracking copies consume the old history before the working state is overwritten. Unified-pool strides and the Inkling convolution channel axis are preserved. Flattened attention padding is cropped before grouping rows by request.

## Test Plan

- 13 checks passed on four GB300 GPUs in 180.09 seconds, including cold compilation: dense/strip numerical parity, padded-slot isolation, tracking order, graph replay with changed inputs, allocation/reservation accounting, unified-pool allocation and strided commit, fused attention writer, and fused all-reduce writer.
- Recurring coverage contains 12 cases, six requiring one GPU. The four-GPU fused all-reduce comparison was an ad hoc run and is not registered in CI. The new CI estimate is 90 seconds; the fused attention writer took 51.906 seconds including cold compilation, while the ad hoc four-GPU check took 103.021 seconds.
- Existing memory-budget tests: 7 passed, including 8 subtests.
- Scoped repository formatting/lint hooks passed. Model-level public Inkling E2E validation remains outstanding; this PR is a draft and keeps the layout opt-in.

records.title: [Fix] Preserve ownership in deep_gemm_wrapper.transform_sf_into_required_layout (FP8 scale use-after-free)
records.body:
## Motivation

`transform_sf_into_required_layout` has the same use-after-free hazard that #32188 fixed for `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor`: sgl-deep-gemm's check-only fast paths (e.g. the FP32 128×128 recipe on SM90) return a **non-owning** `torch::from_blob` alias of the input across the TVM-FFI boundary. Callers rebind the result over their only reference (`param.data = transform_sf_into_required_layout(param.data, ...)`), freeing the storage while DeepGEMM still reads through the alias — observed as NaN weight scales when loading FP8 checkpoints (reported in #39684, root-caused there with a standalone reproducer).

#32188's wrapper guards only `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor`; `transform_sf_into_required_layout` callers are still exposed today.

## Modifications

- Extend the #32188 ownership guard to `transform_sf_into_required_layout` in `deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py`: when the transform returns an alias of the input, hand back the input object itself so ownership is preserved.
- Route the four `srt` call sites through the guarded wrapper: `layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `layers/quantization/mxfp4.py`, `layers/moe/mega_moe.py`, `models/deepseek_v4.py`.
- Add a CUDA regression test (`test/registered/unit/layers/test_deep_gemm_wrapper_ownership.py`) for both guarded wrappers: free the input after the transform, force allocator reuse with NaN-filled sentinel allocations, verify the output is unchanged.

The `sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py` call sites live in the separately-packaged kernels tree and cannot import `srt`; left untouched for a follow-up.

A library-level fix (own-or-clone at the tvm-ffi boundary) has been submitted upstream as sgl-project/DeepGEMM#91; this wrapper mirrors #32188 until that lands in a release, and can be reverted afterwards.

## Accuracy Tests / Benchmark

- Guard logic validated standalone against the published sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.0 wheel on NVIDIA H20 (SM90), torch 2.13.0+cu130: on the alias path the wrapper returns the input object (`out is sf`), and the output survives input-free + allocator-recycle with all values intact; the non-alias path is bit-identical.
- The new regression test fails without the wrapper (output polluted by sentinel NaNs, matching the #39684 reproducer) and passes with it.
- No model-quality or performance impact: the alias path now returns the identical tensor object instead of a dangling alias; all other paths are unchanged (zero-copy).

- [x] Format your code according to the contributor guide (self-reviewed; happy to run the project's pre-commit on request)
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the running tests documentation
- [ ] Update documentation — not needed; behavior-only fix with docstrings

records.title: [Diffusion][XPU] Enable the packed Ulysses QKV all-to-all on XPU
records.body:
The packed-QKV input exchange was gated to CUDA by `is_cuda` checks in the relayout kernel and in both eligibility predicates, so XPU silently fell back to three separate collectives per attention layer and never populated the A2A staging cache.

Nothing on this path is CUDA-specific: the pack is an in-tree Triton kernel and the exchange is `all_to_all_single`. Relax those gates to a device-type set; "cuda" also covers ROCm, where `is_cuda` is True, so ROCm is unchanged.

Two CUDA-only calls on the same path had to move to `torch.get_device_module()`, which is exactly `torch.cuda` for a CUDA device:

- `_a2a_staging_buffer` called `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`, which raises `RuntimeError: Tried to instantiate dummy base class` on an XPU-only build rather than returning False. It was unreachable only because the `device.type != "cuda"` test short-circuited ahead of it, so relaxing the device gate alone would have crashed.
- `drop_a2a_staging_buffers` guarded its synchronize on `torch.cuda.is_available()`, so on XPU it cleared the cache without waiting for collectives that may still be reading those buffers. Dormant until this change populated the cache on XPU. Its call site in `gpu_worker.py` already excludes only CPU/MPS and calls `torch.get_device_module().empty_cache()`.

Tests: resolve the accelerator once per module instead of hardcoding `device="cuda"`, so the six cases run on XPU as well; CUDA is probed first so a CUDA host keeps identical coverage. Add
`test_packed_path_issues_one_collective` -- the unpacked fallback is also bit-exact, so the equivalence test passes whether or not the packed path was selected, and only the collective count pins the device gate.

records.title: [unified-memory] Derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes (1/7)
records.body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 1/7 — derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes

Base: `main`. 7 commits, 21 files, +733/−118.

## The problem

A per-layer K/V buffer is not always a contiguous `[slots, heads, head_dim]` tensor. The
unified memory pool hands out per-layer *views* into one page envelope, and such a view's
slot stride can exceed `heads * head_dim`.

Two things then go wrong, and **neither raises**:

- a consumer that computes a slot address from the tensor's **shape** addresses the wrong
  slot;
- a `.contiguous()` on such a view makes a private copy instead of aliasing the live pool,
  so writes land somewhere the kernels never read.

This PR fixes the sglang-side sites that did either. **On contiguous buffers every change
is a no-op**, so behaviour on today's pools is unchanged — which is why it ships first and
alone.

## What changes

Every sglang-side consumer that derived a KV row address from a tensor's **shape** now
derives it from the tensor's **stride**, and every gate that tested `is_contiguous()` as a
proxy for "addressable" now tests the property the kernel actually requires.

That covers three kinds of site: the pool's slot-stride table, which feeds the slot-move
engine; the write and fused-quantisation kernels, which step by a destination slot stride
instead of assuming a packed row; and the canary/debug sources, which alias the live layer
view rather than snapshotting a copy of it. The canary launch accepts such a view (it needs
packed rows, not a contiguous tensor), and checks a source's row *width*, not its stride,
against the bytes it is asked to hash — the bytes past a strided row's end belong to another
layer.

The tiled slot-move copy uses the slot stride as its copy width too, so it is only correct on
contiguous buffers. `_init_kv_copy_and_warmup` now asserts `is_contiguous()`: a strided pool
that turns the copy on fails at startup instead of spilling into the neighbouring slot. (The unified pool
builds its sub-pools with the copy off.)

The HiCache host pools (MHA and MLA) take the device row stride from the device buffers too,
instead of passing the row width as the device-side stride. A backup of strided rows goes
through the JIT all-layer kernel with that stride — for a `page_first` host as well, instead
of the staged write-back, which reads whole device pages — and the AOT transfer kernels,
which step device rows by the row width, refuse strided rows. The JIT per-layer load already
read the device tensor's stride. A pool whose device rows are packed records nothing and
behaves as before.

One stride helper is narrowed as part of this: it rebuilt every stride from the sizes, which
silently turned a strided view into a contiguous description of itself.

Four CUDA `.cuh` kernels gain a stride parameter. That is the one part of this PR whose blast
radius is not confined to Python, and it is the reason this lands first and by itself.

## Why this is worth its own PR

It is pure hardening: it fixes a class of bug (address derived from shape, not stride)
that is *latent today* and becomes reachable the moment a pool hands out strided views —
which is exactly what 3/7 does. Landing it separately means the layout change that makes
these paths live does not also have to carry their fixes.

## Tests

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_stride_hygiene.py` — CPU, pins each Python-side
  behaviour on a deliberately strided buffer, including the slot-move copy's contiguity
  check and the canary's row-width check.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kv_canary/test_verify_hand.py`, `test_write_hand.py` — GPU,
  strided real-KV sources (the fixtures' `row_gap`) through the CUDA-vs-reference
  differential, so the kernels are shown to step rows by `stride(0)`.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_masked_set_kv_buffer_strided.py` — GPU, builds a
  buffer whose slot stride exceeds one K row via `as_strided` and asserts writes land at the
  slot stride. A hardcoded `loc * H * D` writes into the wrong slot **without any error**, so
  this test is the only thing that can catch a regression here.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache.py` — GPU, the strided
  fp8 path.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_strided_device_rows.py` — GPU,
  round-trips strided device rows through the MHA host pool (`layer_first` and
  `page_first`) and compares them bit for bit; stepping device rows by the row width copies
  neighbouring bytes instead.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+0.79%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.25 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

records.body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 2/7 — build paged KV views through one helper

Base: #40326 (1/7). 6 commits, 13 files, +704/−47.

## The problem

Attention backends turn a per-layer `[slots, heads, head_dim]` buffer into the
`[num_pages, page_size, heads, head_dim]` form their paged kernels take with ad-hoc
`.view(-1, page_size, H, D)` calls. Splitting dim 0 keeps the slot stride as dim 1's
stride — **except at `page_size == 1`**, where `.view()` gives the size-1 dim the *row*
stride, which differs from the slot stride as soon as the per-layer buffer is strided.

Each site also re-derives the shape from the layer's config, and nothing states the stride
contract.

## What changes

Three helpers in a new `mem_cache/layout/paged_view.py`, and every pool-buffer page split in
the paged backends routed through them.

### Which helper to use

This is the rule a new backend should follow; it is the whole API surface:

| you hold | the kernel wants | use |
|---|---|---|
| a **raw MHA pool buffer** from `get_kv_buffer` — rank you do not control (3-D slot-major under NHD, 4-D already-paged under HND) | `[pages, ps, H, D]` | **`paged_kv_view(buf, ps, H, D)`** |
| a tensor **already shaped** the way the kernel wants its rows | same rows, pages split | **`paged_view(t, ps)`** |
| the same, but the kernel wants each row **flat** | `[pages, ps, row_elems]` | **`paged_row_view(t, ps)`** |

In one line: **`paged_kv_view` when the pool hands you the buffer; `paged_view` when you
have already shaped the rows; `paged_row_view` when the kernel takes a flat row.**

`paged_view` is the primitive — it builds the paged view from the buffer's own strides, so
dim 1 carries the slot stride at every page size. The other two differ only in how they
prepare rows before calling it: `paged_row_view` *is* `paged_view(flat.view(slots, -1), ps)`,
and `paged_kv_view` is `paged_view` with a row reshape to `[H, D]`, plus the HND case,
where it only swaps the head and token dims of the already-paged buffer. Only `paged_kv_view` knows about HND, because it is the only one receiving a buffer
whose rank it did not choose.

fa3 shows the contrast within 400 lines: the paged MHA cache calls `paged_kv_view` on the
raw buffer, while the cascade path does `.view(-1, H, D)` itself and then calls
`paged_view`, because it has already shaped its rows and only needs page-size-one blocks.

### Sites routed

Every pool-buffer page split in the paged backends now goes through one of the three
helpers — the MHA caches and the fused rope store through `paged_kv_view`, the MLA latent
and rope caches through `paged_view`, and the MLA backends whose kernels take a flat row
through `paged_row_view`. Each site keeps the page size it used before, including the case
where a draft worker's pool pages at a multiple of the backend's own.

Two shapes are deliberately left alone: a regrouping path that needs a contiguous page block
and raises rather than mis-addresses, and row views built inside stride-aware kernel wrappers
on their own arguments.

## Behaviour

On pools without strided views every site produces the same tensor as before — shape,
strides and storage offset — for NHD, fp8, nvfp4 and MLA buffers at any page size, and for
HND buffers with one KV head.

HND buffers with more than one KV head (`SGLANG_USE_HND_KVCACHE`) change, from wrong to
right. The old `.view(-1, ps, H, D)` only relabelled a `[pages, H, ps, D]` buffer's bytes,
swapping heads with in-page tokens, while `set_kv_buffer` writes true HND. `paged_kv_view`
now returns `buf.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)`, so fa3 reads the tokens that were written, and
trtllm_mha's own permute hands its kernel the HND buffer itself. The HND pools in use today
fold heads into pages and have one KV head, where both forms agree.

The one exception: fa3's absorbed-MLA views, whose size-1 dims (the single KV head, and the
page dim at `page_size 1`) now record a different stride. An index into a size-1 dim is
always 0, so this cannot change addressing; it is visible only to a kernel that reads that
stride.

## Tests

- `test_trtllm_mha_paged_kv.py` — pins the row-then-page order on strided packed and flat
  rows (at `page_size == 1` the `.view()` form gives the size-1 page dim the row stride), and
  that an HND buffer reaches the kernel head for head and token for token.
- `test_flashattention_paged_mha.py` — pins the paged MHA cache's page size, the HND
  head/token mapping, and the `head_group_num` refusal on a strided view.
- `test_paged_view.py` — pins the helpers' strides, including `page_size == 1`, and
  `paged_kv_view`'s HND mapping.
- `test/registered/attention/test_trtllm_mha_stride_parity.py`, `test_trtllm_mla_stride_parity.py`
  — SM100, registered on `4-gpu-b200`. Identical page contents go through a contiguous cache
  and through an over-strided view (slot stride widened to a whole entry), and the outputs
  must be bit-identical (`torch.equal`): trtllm-gen MHA decode and context with bf16 and fp8
  KV, and MLA decode through `paged_row_view` on trtllm_mla, cutedsl_mla and tokenspeed_mla.
  All pass on B200.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+0.87%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.50 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

## End to end

These paths first see strided views in 3/7; #38592 lists the end-to-end runs of each
admitted SM100 backend under `--enable-unified-memory`, on top of the parity tests above.

records.title: [unified-memory] Mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door (4/7)
records.body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 4/7 — mark the write loc physical, and check the mark at every write door

Base: #38592 (3/7). 9 commits, 45 files, +935/−132.

## Why

A unified pool's write door needs physical token ids. The allocator hands out virtual ids,
and `KVIndexTranslator.rebind_write_loc` translates the batch's write loc at `ForwardBatch`
construction; every other pool allocates physically, so the two coincide. Under 3/7's
token-major views a virtual id is in range and, by value, the same kind of integer as a
physical one, so a loc that skipped the rebind writes to the wrong slots without any error.
3/7 deletes the only probe that could tell them apart, because the new layout makes it
vacuous. This PR replaces it with an explicit mark, checked at every write door.

## The contract

| piece | role |
|---|---|
| `ForwardBatch.out_cache_loc_is_physical` | the batch's write loc holds physical ids. `rebind_write_loc` sets it on every pool, translating or not; the capture-time and draft-runner constructors that build a batch outside `init_new` set it themselves |
| `KVWriteLoc.physical` | carries the mark to the pool; `False` unless stated |
| `KVWriteLoc.for_batch(forward_batch, *, swa_loc, full_loc)` | the batch's `out_cache_loc` with the batch's mark. It wraps nothing else, because the mark describes that tensor only |
| `KVWriteLoc.for_layer(forward_batch, layer, …)` | the same, except that a cross-attention layer gets `encoder_out_cache_loc`, which nothing translates and so is never marked |
| `KVCache.requires_physical_write_loc` | set by the unified pools. Their write doors raise `ValueError` on a loc not marked physical. The check is a flag read with no device sync, so it runs on every write-door call. Fused writers that scatter through `get_kv_buffer`, and a replayed cuda graph, do not pass through a door |

A loc produced separately states its own mark with `KVWriteLoc(loc, physical=…)`:
trtllm_mla's capture-stable decode buffer (the runner translates into it), triton's
rank-local DCP slot of a physical loc, and the dspark / dflash draft writes (draft pools are
always static). `HybridLinearKVPool` and the SWA composites forward the `KVWriteLoc` to their
sub-pools instead of unwrapping it, so the mark reaches the door that checks it.

## Completeness is enforced

`test_physical_write_loc.py` parses every file that can hand a write loc to a pool under
`--enable-unified-memory` — the attention backends on the unified allowlists (tied to
`kv_cache_hook`'s allowed sets, so a newly admitted backend joins the scan) plus `models/`,
`layers/cp/`, `speculative/`, `model_executor/` and `disaggregation/` — and requires the loc
argument of every write-door call to be `KVWriteLoc.for_batch` / `for_layer` or a
`KVWriteLoc(...)` with an explicit `physical=`. It follows local names, parameters and helper
returns, and a self-test shows it flags a bare tensor and an unmarked `KVWriteLoc`. The
adoption covers 44 write-door calls, including fa3's two MLA writes, triton's DCP writes and
the draft-model writes.

The pool side is enforced the same way. Producers now hand a `KVWriteLoc` to every pool,
static ones included, so the same file also requires every `set_kv_buffer` /
`set_mla_kv_buffer` override under `srt/` to unwrap its loc argument, forward it untouched to
another door, take only `*args`, or only raise. It covers 30 doors.

## When a new backend must wrap

If the backend can receive a unified pool, its write doors pass
`KVWriteLoc.for_batch(forward_batch, …)`, or `for_layer` when it serves cross-attention. If
it translates the ids itself, it passes `KVWriteLoc(loc, physical=True)`. The ratchet above
fails otherwise.

## Static-pool paths the new loc type reaches

Wrapping the loc changes what static pools and backends receive, not just unified ones:

- triton with `--dcp-size > 1` compares `positions.numel()` with the rank-local loc's length;
  it now reads the wrapped tensor (`loc.loc.numel()`). `test_dcp_layout_unit.py` drives the
  DCP write with a stub pool.
- `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4.set_mla_kv_buffer`, `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool`'s two doors,
  `LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool.set_mla_kv_buffer` and
  `PageInterleaveMLATokenToKVPool.set_mla_kv_buffer` take `loc_info` and unwrap it, like
  their siblings.
- Hand-built batch stubs that drive a write path carry `out_cache_loc_is_physical`
  (`test_cp_strategy_unit.py`, `test_fused_fp8_kv_write.py`).

On the H200, before the stack was rebased onto current main, each against the base it then had
(0318a8d0af) (GSM8K 5-shot, n=200):

| model | configuration | base | without these fixes | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | tp2, dcp2, triton | 0.855 | `AttributeError` at the first KV write | 0.835 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `fp4_mx_block16` KV cache, flashinfer, `--max-total-tokens 262144` | 0.175 | `AttributeError` in graph capture | 0.180 |

DeepSeek-V2-Lite is a base model: with a bf16 KV cache on the same setup it scores
0.325, so the FP4 rows are to be read against each other. The token cap keeps
flashinfer's FP4 decode, which dequantizes the whole pool, inside memory at both commits.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+1.03%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.50 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

Against the preceding PR's run on the same matrix the median per-model shift is −0.11 pp —
this PR moves nothing.

## End to end with the always-on check

Each run below boots with `--enable-unified-memory` and writes through the checked doors;
none refuses a write (GSM8K 5-shot, n=100). The unified-vs-baseline comparison for these
backends is in #38592.

| box | model | backend | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|
| H200 | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | fa3 | 0.890 |
| B200 | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | trtllm_mla | 0.900 |
| B200 | Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | cutedsl_mla | 0.890 |
| B200 | Qwen3.5-9B, tp1, cuda graphs off | trtllm_mha | 0.900 |

aiter's write doors are marked, but aiter is not admitted under `--enable-unified-memory`, so
the ratchet does not scan it, and its doors have not been run on ROCm.

# 5/7 — remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing

Base: #40328 (4/7). 5 commits, 17 files, **+117/−230**.

## What and why

3/7 pinned `kernel_page_multiplier` to 1: under the token-major entry a kernel-facing id
*is* the physical token id, so there is no per-page block scale left for an id to carry.
This PR deletes the plumbing that existed only to carry it.

Pure deletion. **Nothing left behind computes differently** — every site either multiplied
by a value that is now always 1, or passed it along.

What goes: the multiplier's keyword arguments and properties across the unified
allocators and the index translator, the `* mult` at every use site, the stride arguments
that existed only to re-derive the scaled id, and the corresponding parameters in the
kernels that took them. The read-table build loses its scaling step and reduces to a
clamped table lookup. The aiter MLA backend's DCP verify path passed the multiplier to
`create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp` too; it now passes the same arguments as trtllm_mla's.
The write-loc translate kernel's `stride` argument goes as well: its one caller passed the
page size, so the kernel computes `phys * page_size + offset` itself. The translator's module
doc now describes two id spaces, virtual and physical.

Both translate implementations are **left untouched** here. With the multiplier gone,
`translate_kv_loc` and `translate_kv_loc_for_kernel` compute the same id for any in-range
non-negative input, differing only in implementation (several torch ops vs one Triton
launch) and in how they treat a negative loc. Folding them is **6/7** — kept separate so
this PR carries no behaviour change at all.

## Why it is not merged into 3/7

They are different kinds of change, and the split is deliberate:

- 3/7 is the feature, and its middle commit is where a reviewer must think hard. Seventeen
  files of deletion would dilute exactly the focus the split was made to create.
- They are **independently revertible**. If this removal turns out to break a consumer we did
  not find, reverting it alone leaves the layout intact — and the layout is what 4/7, 6/7,
  7/7 and downstream work all stand on. Merged, that revert would take the layout with it.

## Review shape

Net −113 lines across 17 files, eight of them tests whose edits follow the removal; test
cases that only exercised a multiplier above 1 are converted to the page-size form or
dropped, and the two single-full-attention-layer tests (the multiplier-1 case), which the
removal turned into duplicates, are folded into the general ones. Checking this PR is
mostly confirming that every deleted argument was provably 1.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+1.30%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **+0.00 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

The median per-model perf shift against the preceding PR's run is −0.09 pp.

## End to end

The admitted SM100 backends were run with unified memory at the stack tip; see #40331.

>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>

> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 6/7 — stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it

Base: #40329 (5/7). 5 commits, 11 files, +361/−159.

## Why

`main` computes `v2p[t // ps] * ps + t % ps` in two places: the fused Triton kernel
(`_translate_loc_fused`, used by the read table, the SWA read and the write translate) and a
torch body (`translate_kv_loc`, used by the composites and the PD / HiCache transfer
translates). They disagree on the ids nobody looks at: the torch body faults on a negative or
past-the-table id and on 2-D input, while the kernel sends them to the page-0 sink. The
kernel could not take every caller, because it flat-addresses its input and so needs it
contiguous, while the SWA read path hands down `page_table[:bs, :max_seq_len]`, a column
slice of the capture-stable buffer.

## Commit 1 — walk the kernel by its strides

`loc` and `out` are walked as a `(rows, cols)` view with row and column strides passed per
launch. The decomposition sits behind a `STRIDED` constexpr, so a contiguous pair still takes
the flat path with no div/mod; that is what the per-forward write translate under cuda-graph
capture uses.

- **The strides are runtime arguments, not `tl.constexpr`.** A page table's live width
  changes every few decode steps, and a constexpr stride would recompile with it.
- **Offsets are computed in int64.** A row stride times a row count can exceed 2^31, and an
  int32 overflow here would mis-address silently.
- **`out_width` stays on the flat path, by assert.** That mode writes a packed lane range
  `[0, W)` with a zero tail; a non-contiguous 1-D `loc` would send the tail lanes over the
  live prefix, so the assert is load-bearing.
- The `out=None` allocation no longer mirrors a strided `loc`, so the caller gets a
  contiguous result.

## Commit 2 — one implementation

`translate_kv_loc` calls the fused kernel, and the torch body and `translate_kv_loc_for_kernel`
are deleted. For the callers that were on the torch path — the composites' `translate_kv_loc`,
the PD transfer translates, retraction's `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy` and
`_materialize_inflight_write_set` (HiCache's transfer translate was already on the kernel) — a negative or past-the-table id now resolves to the
page-0 sink instead of faulting; 2-D, int32 and strided inputs are accepted; and each call is
one launch instead of up to six. Trading a fault for the sink is deliberate: these calls can
run inside a captured graph, where a device-side assert is not a diagnostic. Paths already on
the fused kernel — the read table, the SWA read, the pool's FULL→SWA — do not change, and
every id the torch body accepted translates to the same value.

## Tests

- `test_matches_reference_on_a_strided_view` and `test_translate_accepts_a_strided_page_table`
  fail on 5/7 (`loc must be contiguous`) and pass here.
- `test_a_loc_past_the_sentinel_lands_on_the_sink`, `test_an_out_of_range_loc_lands_on_the_sink`
  and `test_padding_loc_lands_on_the_sink` pin the sink semantics.
- `test_out_width_needs_a_packed_loc` pins the branch that would otherwise regress silently.
- `kernels/ops/memory/test_write_loc_to_kernel_ids_strided.py` (GPU) is the only test that
  enters the kernel, so it is the one that can catch a wrong `row * rs + col * cs`; its oracle
  is the kernel on a contiguous copy, plus the CPU reference. Its lanes cover non-zero
  in-page offsets, the `-1` sink, a tombstoned page, a loc below the sentinel and a page past
  the table, in int32 and int64. Dropping the past-the-table guard or the in-page offset from
  the kernel fails it.

## Validation

A GPU differential of `translate_kv_loc` against the closed-form definition matches in all 114
cases: int32 / int64; page sizes 1, 4, 64; 1-D, 2-D, stride-2, column-slice, transposed and
empty inputs; tombstoned pages; −1, −2, −(ps + 1) and past-the-table locs; `out=None`, packed,
column-slice (neighbours untouched) and in-place `out=`. The 5/7 implementation agrees on all 50
inputs it accepts. `UnifiedSWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa` is one CUDA launch at 5/7,
at this PR and at 7/7.

## Unit tests

At this head on the H200, the strided kernel test and `test_unified_mla_views.py` pass (24
tests), and the kernel test fails when the past-the-table guard or the in-page offset is
removed from the kernel. The stack tip (#40331) was run over the wider unit scope on the H200 and
end to end on B200; see its description.

## Follow-ups this PR does not do

- **Lift the fa3/fa4 local-attention refusal** under `--enable-unified-memory`. Commit 1 removes
  one technical reason for it, but validating the lift needs a local-attention model.
- **Fold the Mamba id translate.** `UnifiedMambaPool.translate` is still a plain torch gather; at
  page size 1 it computes the same value but does not clamp, so a tombstoned row returns `-1`
  rather than the sink.

records.title: [unified-memory] Name the fused KV translate for what it computes (7/7)
records.body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 7/7 — name the fused KV translate for what it computes

Base: #40330 (6/7). 5 commits, 28 files, +119/−121.

After 6/7 one kernel serves every KV translate, reads and writes alike, and the kernel-facing
and physical id spaces are the same. The names still said otherwise. This PR renames, with no
behaviour change:

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `write_loc_to_kernel_ids` / `write_loc_to_kernel_id_kernel` / `WRITE_LOC_BLOCK` | `translate_token_ids` / `translate_token_ids_kernel` / `TRANSLATE_TOKEN_IDS_BLOCK` |
| `translate_write_loc_for_kernel` (sub-allocator and composites) | `translate_write_loc` |
| `_assert_kernel_id_bound` | `_assert_physical_id_bound` |
| `test_write_loc_to_kernel_ids_strided.py` | `test_translate_token_ids_strided.py` |

The kernel registry entry, callers and tests follow. The kernel's argument comments now
describe its real inputs (1-D or strided `(rows, cols)`, int32 or int64, widened under DCP), an
unreachable 0-d branch goes, and the allocator docstrings say "physical" where they said
"kernel-facing".

Comments follow the identifiers: every comment, docstring and unified-memory error message
that called these ids "kernel-facing" now says "physical". Left alone are the sites that
state the equivalence on purpose, one that describes a historical bug, and two where the
word means something else (the Mamba checkpoint pool, the communicator). Three
descriptions that were wrong are corrected: the kernel's `out` under `out_width`, the
parity test's page-major formula, and the inkling test's account of a re-translated loc.

The first commit is a scripted mechanical rename; the next two are comments and the two
identifier renames; the last two are the corrections and the comment sweep, each
droppable on its own.

## Validation

The stack is rebased onto main 047be72a8c; every PR's own diff is unchanged file for file.

Unit and GPU tests on the H200, this head against that main, over every non-e2e test file the stack
touches plus `unit/mem_cache`, `cp`, `dcp`, `unit/layers/attention`, `kernels/ops/memory` and
`kernels/ops/kvcache`: no failure at this head that main does not also have; the extra passes are the
stack's own tests. The server-launching multi-GPU files under `cp/` and `dcp/` error the same way on
both sides on a one-GPU run.

End to end at this head on the H200, unified memory against a baseline on the same model and flags
(GSM8K 5-shot, n=200):

| model | backend | unified | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B, tp1 | triton | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| gpt-oss-20b, tp1 | fa3 | 0.540 | 0.515 |

Before the rebase, at d509377055 — the whole stack — each admitted SM100 backend was run with
unified memory against a baseline on the same model, flags and box (B200, GSM8K 5-shot, n=100):

| model | backend | unified | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B, tp1, cuda graphs off | trtllm_mha | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| gpt-oss-20b, tp1 | fa4 | 0.570 | 0.570 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | trtllm_mla | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2, dcp2, fp8 KV | tokenspeed_mla | 0.930 | 0.930 |

No write was refused by the physical write-loc check and no device-side assert fired. trtllm_mha
without cuda graphs decodes about 7% slower under unified memory, from the translate launches
an eager step adds.

The commits added since that head fix static-pool write doors, tests and comments; none changes a
unified-memory read or write path.

records.title: [diffusion] USP: accept strided row views in the packed QKV all-to-all
records.body: ## Motivation Currently there's support for packing the Q/K/V into one tensor and exchanging them in a single a2a instead of three separate ones in Ulysses. That fast path was gated on all three tensors being fully contiguous, which is stricter than the pack kernel requires: it reads Q/K/V through explicit row and head strides, so only the `head_size` dim needs unit stride. This now exluded many cases. FLUX.2, for example, produces Q/K/V as `qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)`of a merged `to_qkv_mlp_proj` and hands then to attention withhout a `.contiguous()`, so every attention call fell back to three collectives. This PR replaces the contiguous check with one that checks what the kernel needs and routes the remainig call sites through the packed helper. Only data movements changes, output remain indentical. ## Modifications - Add `_packed_qkv_row_view_is_free()`and use it in `_can_use_packed_qkv_a2a_4d()`in place of the three `is_contiguous()` checks. - Route the replicated-prefix and replicated-suffix USP paths through `_usp_input_all_to_all_qkv` instead of three separate a2a. For ineligible layouts this helpers falls back to the three separate calls. - Add predicate tests: the FLUX.2 layout (chunk of a merged projection) is accepted and its row view verified copy-free; `b > 1` sliced along seq is rejected, since merging batch and seq there would copy; contiguous input is unchanged; a gapped head dim is rejected. ## Accuracy Tests Command: ``` sglang generate \ --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev \ --num-gpus 8 --ulysses-degree 8 --ring-degree 1 \ --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-inference-steps 25 \ --prompt 'A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets' \ --seed 0 \ --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False \ --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False \ --vae-cpu-offload False --offload-during-compile False \ --warmup-mode request --warmup-steps 25 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --output-path /outputs/flux2.pr2 \ --perf-dump-path /outputs/flux2.pr2/perf/pr2.json --save-output" ``` ### Before ### After ## Speed Tests and Profiling #### 1. records.title: Defer serialized CUTLASS NVFP4 scale layouts until loading
records.body:
Serialized CUTLASS NVFP4 models swizzle uninitialized expert scales during construction, then rebuild those layouts after loading. Those duplicate buffers can make a checkpoint fail before its weights are read. MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL on TP2/EP2 RTX PRO 6000 reaches the 95 GiB device limit during audio-encoder construction; the redundant MoE scale buffers account for 8.8125 GiB per rank.

Defer the derived layouts for serialized CUTLASS checkpoints, as the TRTLLM and MegaMoE paths already do. The normal post-load code creates and aliases the populated scales. The online quantization allocation path stays intact.

Validation: five remote CPU tests cover cold allocation, online initialization, post-load values, reloads, and non-gated padding. With this change, the same complete MiMo NVFP4 artifact loads and serves on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell cards, including sampled bring-up, cached conversation and bounded-context checks. No weight or activation precision is changed. The separate MiMo packed-module mapping fix used by that mixed checkpoint is #40675.

Duplicate preflight on 2026-09-22 applies cleanly to upstream 264da633191d. Inspected #38216: it changes FP4 dispatch and per-token all-gather scales, not construction-time derived buffers.

records.title: [AMD] Eliminate remaining gfx95 FP8 scale relayout copies
records.body:
## Motivation

Seven gfx95 block-FP8 producers request row-major scales and then materialize the bpreshuffle layout with an extra GPU copy. This was visible in GLM-5.3 decode as one relayout launch per affected layer. Native `Fp8LinearMethod` checkpoints reach these branches after #39409; block-FP8 implementations exposing `weight_scale` can reach them on current main.

This supersedes #34589 and #24476 with a current-main implementation, based on the approaches from @amd-mvarjoka and @Jacob0226.

## Modifications

Use the existing `emit_transposed_bpreshuffle_scale` gate at the remaining communicator, MLA, and MHA fused-RMS producers. For `M >= 2`, AITER emits the target layout and SGLang applies a zero-copy stride view; `M == 1` keeps the existing materialize path. Extend fused-RMS tests across residual and unquantized-output combinations.

## Accuracy Tests

- Transposed and row-major producer paths are bit-exact for quantized values, scales, residual output, and the DSA bf16 payload.
- GLM-5.3 EAGLE sentinel: 949 samples, mean accept length 3.7189, p50 3.60, with no observed regression.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3 MXFP4, MI355X, TP8, EAGLE 5 steps, concurrency 6 (`M=36`):

- Decode step: 17.175 ms to 16.943 ms (-1.35%), three runs per arm with disjoint ranges.
- Kernel launches: 2078 to 2000 per step; the 78 removed launches match the affected layer count.
- Trace attribution measured the removed relayout copies at 0.297 ms per step.

Measurement: three alternating runs per arm after graph capture/warmup; 50 replays per op, 20 calls per graph.

<details><summary>Commands and local checks</summary>

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_TOPK_MB=1 SGLANG_MQA_VARCTX=1 \
python3 profile_decode.py --tp-size 8 --ep-size 1 \
  --model-path /shared_nfs/models/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --context-length 262144 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --trust-remote-code --max-running-requests 32 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --ISL 100000 --CONC 6

pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/layer_boundary/residual/add_norm.py \
  python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha_rocm.py \
  python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla_rocm.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_fused_rms_fp8_group_quant.py
```

The three methods in `TestFusedRMSFP8GroupQuant` passed in parallel on GPUs 4–6 (four subtests each).

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Documentation is not needed; no user-facing interface changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
