records.title: [Perf] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel, 7 kernels -> 1, 6x speedup on all shapes for this kernel
records.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a kernel-level microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the isolated kernel, both versions in the same process. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing six of seven kernel launches on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency.

## Purpose

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s `"align"` branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request:

```python
start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // kv_cache_spec.block_size
start_indices.clamp_(min=0)
offsets = torch.arange(1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks, ...)
indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
```

The arithmetic is trivial, but as PyTorch ops it is **seven kernel launches** over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor — which holds a **single element** in a one-request decode. Almost all of the cost is launch overhead rather than work.

This is a **shared utility**: `gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call it, so the change is not specific to one model.

## Measured

On MI355X, both versions in the same process so it is like-for-like:

| num_reqs | spec blocks | kernels | us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **7** | **7 -> 1** | **10.81 -> 1.78** | **6.06x** |
| 1 | 3 | 7 -> 1 | 10.91 -> 1.79 | 6.11x |
| 8 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 10.73 -> 1.82 | 5.90x |
| 64 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 12.02 -> 1.95 | 6.16x |

The gain is **flat in batch size**, because the cost is per-launch rather than per-element.

For context on why this site was picked: in a Kimi-K3 concurrency-1 decode trace, attributing every GPU kernel back to its Python call site ranks this the **highest kernels-per-invocation** of any non-model-math site in that model — 7.0 kernels and 19.6 us per invocation. Every other call site in that model is already at or near one kernel per call.

To be explicit about scope: this is a **kernel-level claim**. Against a multi-millisecond decode step it is a fraction of a percent end-to-end, and I am not claiming a measurable throughput change.

## Correctness

**Update after review ([@ChuanLi1101](https://github.com/ChuanLi1101)):** the first version of this kernel indexed the block table as `base + req * stride(0) + start + offs`, which silently assumes a **column stride of 1**. The `torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` it replaces honours any layout, and since this is a shared utility a caller holding a non-contiguous view would have read the wrong blocks. The kernel now takes `block_table.stride(0)`, `block_table.stride(1)` and `seq_lens.stride(0)` explicitly, matching the existing `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` helper.

Worth stating plainly: the original 48-shape sweep below **did not catch this**, because every block table it generated was contiguous. The test added in this PR closes that gap.

Verification now lives in-tree at `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, so CI runs it rather than it being an out-of-tree script. It pins the kernel to the pre-fusion expression over:

- **48 shape combinations** — `num_reqs` 1/2/8/64 x `block_size` 16/64/256 x `num_speculative_blocks` 0/1/3/7, bit-identical (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- **a non-contiguous block table** (`stride(1) == 2`) — the regression test for the bug above
- **`seq_len == 0`**, the CUDA-graph padding row the previous `clamp_(min=0)` guarded, which must clamp to row 0
- **`num_reqs == 0`**, which must not launch a `(0,)` grid
- the **`"all"` / `"none"`** passthrough modes, which still return the input tensor itself rather than a copy

55 tests pass against the fixed kernel. The three non-contiguous cases **fail against the previous kernel**, so the suite catches the defect rather than merely covering the line.

The kernel keeps the same in-range assumption the existing `torch.gather` already relies on: `start + num_speculative_blocks` must lie inside the block-table row.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` — 55 tests, in-tree so CI runs them
- [x] 48 shape combinations bit-identical on device (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- [x] Non-contiguous block table (`stride(1) != 1`) — fails on the pre-fix kernel, passes now
- [x] Edge cases: `num_reqs == 0`, `seq_len == 0` clamp path, `"all"` / `"none"` passthrough
- [x] Timing on MI355X: 7 kernels -> 1, 10.81 us -> 1.78 us (6.06x) at the single-request shape. **Kernel-level only; no end-to-end throughput claim.**
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean

records.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Feed Engram's FP8 rows to wkv without dequant + requant
records.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram table is already MXFP8: FP8 E4M3 rows with one ue8m0 scale per 32 values. The lookup dequantized each row to bf16, and `wkv` (an MXFP8 `[32, 32]` projection, 6144 → 25600) quantized it straight back. This PR hands `wkv` the table's own bytes as a `QuantizedActivation`, so both steps are gone.

- **Unsharded heads** (TP1, or tables shared across DP replicas): the lookup writes the FP8 values into persistent staging, and the scales at their F8_128x4 offsets. `embed()` returns views of those buffers, so no extra kernel runs. Scale rows that pad the last 128-token tile are written as zeros, matching FlashInfer's quantizer.
- **Sharded heads** (TP, or Engram-DP head sharding): each staged row packs its 8 scale bytes after its 256 value bytes. The existing gathers carry this payload unchanged, as one collective per exchange at 264 instead of 512 bytes per head row. `_engram_packed_to_mxfp8` then splits values from scales and swizzles the scales. Under TP it reads the rank-major `dim=0` gather in place, which also drops the `dim=1` gather's `movedim` copy, and it selects the SP token window.
- **When it applies:** only when `wkv`'s kernel is FlashInfer CuTe-DSL or CUTLASS MXFP8, the consumers of F8_128x4 activation scales. The check reuses `can_fuse_query_quant`, the gate of the query RMSNorm + MXFP8 fusion. `K = heads × head_dim` must also be a multiple of 128; DSV4.1 has K = 6144.
- **Everything else is unchanged.** That includes W8A16 Marlin on SM90, which takes bf16 activations and never requantized anything.

**Numerics.** The GEMM output is bit-identical to the previous path. Dequantizing an FP8 row to bf16 is exact. Requantizing it with a ceil-rounded power-of-two scale (FlashInfer's rule) only rescales values by powers of two, without saturating. So the GEMM sees the same real values. `test_engram_mxfp8_rows_match_requantized_wkv` checks this with `atol=0` through the real CuTe-DSL kernel.

### Duplicate-work check

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for `engram`, `engram mxfp8`, `engram wkv`, `engram lookup`, `engram dequant`, `engram requant`, `wkv quant`, and `engram QuantizedActivation`, run on 2026-09-25. None of the related PRs removes the dequant/requant:

- #56989 (draft) packs FP8 rows for the TP exchange, but dequantizes them to bf16 again before `wkv`. It is opt-in, and limited to TP > 1 without SP. This PR never dequantizes on the MXFP8 path, is on by default wherever `wkv` accepts MXFP8, and also covers TP1, SP, and Engram-DP head sharding.
- #56929 (closed, unmerged) quantized the dequantized bf16 rows after the gather. That still paid for both the dequant and the requant.
- #58678 makes `wkv` column-parallel for TP without SP, and #57893 retunes the lookup tiling. Both are compatible with this PR but conflict textually in `common/engram.py`; whichever lands second rebases.

## Test Plan

On a GB300 node (SM103, 4 GPUs), rebased on `22bbe3f102`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <same files>
```

New and extended tests:
- `test_engram_lookup_keeps_mxfp8_bytes`: byte-exact swizzled and packed outputs, from HBM and pinned host memory, at 1, 7, and 130 tokens. The scale buffer is pre-filled with stale bytes, so the zeroed padding rows are actually checked.
- `test_engram_mxfp8_rows_reconstruct_table`: TP 1/2/4 with and without SP, including a padded last head shard.
- `test_engram_mxfp8_rows_match_requantized_wkv`: end-to-end through `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel`, bit-exact against the old path.
- `test_engram_prepared_rows_survive_graph_breaks` and the 2-GPU `test_engram_head_collectives_survive_graph_breaks` now also run the MXFP8 path. This covers CPU-offload prefetch; eager, compiled, full, and breakable CUDA-graph capture; and real TP all-gathers.

## Test Result

- **Tests:** 139 passed, 0 skipped, including the 2-GPU test.
- **Checks:** pre-commit and mypy pass.
- **Kernel microbenchmark** (GB300; 24 heads × 256; random ids into a 16M-row table; CUDA-graph timing). "Old" is lookup + `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` as `wkv` ran it. The TP4 columns are one rank's local kernels, with the collective excluded:

| tokens | TP1, table in HBM: old → new (µs) | TP4 local kernels: old → new (µs) | TP1, table on host: requant removed from main stream (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.1 → 1.8 | 3.8 → 3.1 | 1.5 |
| 128 | 4.1 → 2.2 | 7.0 → 3.5 | 1.6 |
| 1024 | 12.4 → 6.2 | 19.6 → 5.5 | 4.4 |
| 4096 | 60.2 → 20.4 | 89.8 → 15.3 | 12.4 |
| 16384 | 281.6 → 176.2 | 333.5 → 87.3 | 49.7 |

With the table offloaded to host (the default), the lookup still runs on the prefetch stream at unchanged cost. The gain is the requant leaving the main stream, for each of the two Engram layers. At TP4, each exchange moves 48% fewer bytes.

- **Model evaluation:** pending; this PR stays a draft until the GSM8K and GPQA results for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, GB300) are added here.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation, tests, benchmarks, and this description. The human submitter is accountable for the change.

records.title: [Perf] Fuse MiMo partial RoPE, value scaling, and packed DiffKV writes
records.body:
## Purpose

MiMo's DiffKV attention prepares partial RoPE, scales V, and writes the packed KV cache in separate steps. This change combines that preparation into one Triton kernel for unquantized CUDA DiffKV attention, returning a fresh rotated Q while preserving the input QKV allocation. It supports the MiMo V2.6 QK192/V128 layout with rotary width 64 and retains the existing attention wrapper and backend.

The model selects this path for stock rotary embeddings with FA-DiffKV or Triton-DiffKV, FP16/BF16 storage, and DCP=1. Other configurations keep the existing path. Cache addressing uses actual strides and 64-bit token/head arithmetic; padded or negative slots skip stores while still producing Q.

Related work covers different operations: #58128 handles FP8/config propagation, #58177 prefill tiling, and #58141 multi-token split-KV. The standard-attention fusion in #57271 and #52363 does not cover MiMo's QK192/V128 layout, partial rotary width 64, and V scaling. #47535 and #52468 optimize standalone cache writes. This change combines rotary, scaling and cache writes; its measurements do not isolate the benefit remaining after a future merge of those writer optimizations.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k rope_and_cache_diffkv -v
.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.kernels.benchmark_mimo_rope_cache --backend both --output mimo-rope-cache.json
```

The benchmark compares native Inductor RoPE/V scaling (`combo_kernels=True`, `benchmark_combo_kernel=True`) plus the existing cache writer against the fused kernel, with the same attention consumer. It records alternating A/B/A controls, eight rounds, and eight calls per captured CUDA Graph. Samples have warm intra-sample L2 and exclude projections, metadata construction and model serving.

## Test Result

On one Modal NVIDIA B200, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / Triton 3.7.1:

- All four added repository tests passed, using C++ rotary plus the existing cache writer as the exact reference. The isolated run used `--noconftest`; no full repository suite or upstream CI pass is claimed.
- A separate correctness harness passed 12 BF16/FP16 configurations, both rotary layouts, partial-width tails, offset/strided inputs and cache, shortened/negative slot maps, and CUDA Graph replays with changed metadata. A physical 6.60 GB allocation crossed a 3.3-billion-element head offset with exact output/store/guard checks.
- Six actual `MiMoV2Attention` cases with random QKV/output projections passed on both backends, including graph replay with changed buffers. The compiled case was bitwise equal; eager native BF16 produced small expected intermediate-rounding differences within the declared tolerances. Schema, FakeTensor and AOT dynamic opchecks passed.
- All 16 final benchmark cases had bitwise-equal Q, cache and attention outputs. A CPU source-contract probe checked 15 dispatch configurations and the profiling/fake paths; this does not claim distributed runtime coverage. All applicable pre-commit checks passed.

Final FA4 results (the automatically selected DiffKV implementation on this B200), median microseconds:

| Case | Native | Fused | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Full decode, KV32K, Q/KV64/4 | 35.662 | 33.216 | 1.074x |
| SWA128 decode, batch 1, Q/KV64/8 | 10.762 | 7.993 | 1.346x |
| SWA128 decode, batch 8, Q/KV64/8 | 12.029 | 8.454 | 1.423x |
| SWA128 decode, batch 64, Q/KV8/1 | 11.786 | 8.460 | 1.393x |
| Full verify, batch 4 x query 8, KV4096 | 54.193 | 51.104 | 1.060x |
| SWA128 prefill, query 256, KV512 | 28.978 | 22.066 | 1.313x |
| SWA128 prefill, query 2048, KV4096 | 156.643 | 122.864 | 1.275x |
| SWA128 prefill, query 8192, KV8192 | 592.329 | 456.829 | 1.297x |

FA4 A/A control ratios ranged from 0.988 to 1.021; using the faster baseline control, the batch-8 speedup is 1.394x. Explicit Triton-DiffKV also improved in all eight tested cases, with larger SWA gains than the 1–2% full-attention differences. Its largest A/A difference was 4.65%, so small changes should be interpreted with that control in view.

These are bounded attention-path measurements, not model E2E or service-throughput results. The GPU environment used pinned prebuilt vLLM binaries (`0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8`) with the tested current Python sources overlaid; it was not a full fresh build of main. No full model weights were downloaded. H100, GB10, multi-rank DCP and quantized caches were not benchmarked.

Implementation and validation were AI-assisted.

records.title: [KV Cache] Support hidden-state extraction with packed BLHNC layouts
records.body:
## Purpose

Addresses [#59024](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59024): Enable GLM-5.3-Flash hidden-state extraction through the API used by Speculators, while preserving the model's packed BLHNC cache layout. 

## Background

This branch follows the plan in #59024: 
* it builds on the generic packed KV-cache layout from [#57169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57169), and 
* incorporates GLM auxiliary-state capture from [#56983](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56983).
Once those PRs are merged, the changes can be removed from this PR.

Changes in this PR: size hidden-state cache pages as to fit the existing packed layout, and let the connector read strided views instead of requiring LBNHC.

Full-model validation also exposed a graph-selection gap: MRV2 disabled CUDA graphs because its fallback recognized torch.compile-based piecewise execution but missed GLM's breakable graphs. The fix makes MRV2 report that capability, allowing automatic fallback to piecewise graphs.

## Validation

Tested MRV2 with the full GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint on four B300 GPUs, using Speculators' actual launcher and HTTP client.

- 40 requests passed without forcing a graph mode.
- 20 saved outputs matched references from the same execution byte-for-byte; every checked chunk replayed graphs.
- Covered mixed lengths, chunk boundaries, repeated requests, and identical prompts. No batch-invariance assumption.
- 10 graph-mode resolver tests and lint, formatting, and Python 3.12 type checks passed. Earlier validation also passed 136 cache/connector unit tests.

Scope: text prompts, layers 5/22/43/45, prefix caching disabled. Generated-token extraction and performance remain unvalidated.

Implementation and validation used AI assistance.

records.title: [Attention] Support FlashInfer re-paging for packed BLHNC KV caches
records.body:
## Purpose

Enable FlashInfer dense GQA to use packed BLHNC KV caches with BF16/FP16 storage.

Manager blocks remain intact while FlashInfer reads smaller kernel pages through remapped indices and shared-storage views. This enables the existing packed grouping for configurations such as Qwen3.6 + DFlash, reducing KV groups from 46 to 5. The change also aligns ordinary sliding-window manager blocks with the primary attention block size.

Addresses question 2 in #58638. This complements #58380's layout selection and the sparse MLA work in #55219/#57169; it adds the dense FlashInfer read path without depending on #57169.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  -k 'packed_flashinfer or sliding_window_keeps_manager_size or packed_allocation_retains_manager_blocks or clear_layer_kv_caches_releases_flashinfer_read_views'
```

Serving setup:
- 1× B300, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.0.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash.
- MRv2, TP=1, FlashInfer, BF16 activation/KV/Mamba states, 7 speculative tokens.
- Max model length 262144, max sequences 32, max batched tokens 8192, block size 128, GPU memory utilization 0.8.
- Chunked prefill enabled; prefix caching disabled for throughput tests.
- `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`.

Both layouts use this branch. Each layout was tested on two fresh servers in alternating order. The workloads below used 8/8/32 warmup requests and 256/64/256 measured requests. Performance uses synthetic acceptance length 4; accuracy uses real speculative verification.

## Test Result

**8 focused regression cases passed**, covering graph replay, packed/dense read equivalence, manager-sized allocation, cache cleanup and SWA block sizing. Ruff and format checks passed.

Runtime checks confirmed that target and draft attention use the new path: **640-token manager blocks, 128-token kernel pages, shared storage**.

**Serving results**, averaged over two independent runs per layout:

| Workload | Metric | LBHNC | BLHNC | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 input / 1 output, c1 | req/s | 6.419 | 7.015 | **+9.3%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c1 | output tok/s | 286.56 | 427.01 | **+49.0%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c32 | output tok/s | 5115.53 | 7221.04 | **+41.2%** |
| 8192 input / 1 output, c1 | p99 TTFT, ms | 160.59 | 148.02 | **−7.8%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c1 | p99 TPOT, ms | 3.478 | 2.328 | **−33.1%** |
| 1024 input / 1024 output, c32 | p99 TPOT, ms | 6.038 | 4.274 | **−29.2%** |

The two c32 runs measured **7258.52** and **7183.57 tok/s**, improving over their paired LBHNC runs by **42.0%** and **40.3%**.

KV groups dropped **46→5**. Reported KV capacity increased **6,640,889→6,789,922 tokens (+2.2%)**, with comparable peak PyTorch allocated memory: **214.281→214.263 GiB**.

**NSYS**, 32 steady decode steps:

| Per-step measurement | LBHNC | BLHNC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Target metadata scope | 8.948 ms | 1.632 ms |
| Scheduler scope | 3.575 ms | 0.789 ms |
| GPU activity gaps | 16.542 ms | 7.521 ms |

The trace shows that enabling packed grouping reduces repeated metadata construction and scheduling work, allowing the GPU to spend less time waiting between operations.

**Correctness:**
- GSM8K, 250 questions, 5-shot chat, thinking disabled: **244/250 (97.6%)** for both layouts, with identical response texts.
- Real mean acceptance length: **5.297733** for both layouts.
- Fixed-prompt cold-cache and block-reuse checks: exact logits and greedy-token matches. Prefix-hit checks also produced identical greedy tokens.
- Two-GPU DCP kernel validation: **12 cases passed**, including BF16/FP16, empty local shards, partial pages and graph replay. Maximum output/LSE errors were **0.00862 / 1.91e-6**.

E2E/profiling measurements used `fb780b9b0`; the final guard simplification passed six routing-equivalence checks.

records.title: [KV Offload] Preserve packed layouts for layer-wise KV cache
records.body:
## Purpose

Fourth follow-up to #56155, #56156, and #56116; related RFC: #57445.
Depends on #56116. The incremental change is commit
[`bed877a176`](https://github.com/meenchen/vllm/commit/bed877a176):
**5 production lines**, regression tests, and documentation. The cumulative
GitHub diff includes the prerequisite stack while those PRs remain open.
Review only this follow-up with the
[incremental comparison](https://github.com/meenchen/vllm/compare/layerwise-mixed-kv-packed-hybrid...layerwise-kv-offloading).

`OffloadingConnector` currently requests `LBHNC`, which bypasses the packed
hybrid allocator. On Nemotron-3-Nano with three FP8 K/V and three NVFP4 K/V
layers, this selects a 1,088-token padded manager page and fails at startup:

```text
block stride 557056 != page 156672
a manager block cannot be split into 17 kernel blocks of 64 tokens
```

For quantization configurations advertising `has_layerwise_kv_cache()`, let the
allocator select the layout. The existing packed-row offload implementation
then handles KV payloads, quantization scales, and state bytes without format
conversion. Non-layerwise configurations keep `LBHNC`; HiSparse keeps `BLHNC`.
No transfer kernels or scheduler behavior change.

## Test Result

On 4x GB300, exact stacked Python sources plus the nightly wheel's native
extensions (`0.29.1rc1.dev513+g0961bbae2`, Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer
`0.6.18.post1`):

- Exact-source baseline reproduced the startup failure above.
- Candidate Nano TP4: FULL and PIECEWISE CUDA graphs captured; both FlashInfer
  FP8 and NVFP4 KV paths resolved.
- After GPU prefix-cache reset, the CPU tier reloaded 83,226,624 bytes and reused
  1,024 tokens from a 1,081-token prompt. All 128 generated token IDs and finite
  log probabilities matched cold generation exactly. Clearing both cache tiers
  and recomputing also matched exactly. Workers exited gracefully.
- Byte-exact GPU/CPU round trips cover mixed FP8/NVFP4 rows, attention-only and
  attention/Mamba layouts, multiple destination block IDs, and offload chunks
  containing one or three GPU blocks.
- Broad regression suite on the final fixture: **541 passed, 1 skipped**
  (ROCm-only), including the existing non-layerwise tests.
- Full repository pre-commit passed, including mypy 3.10 and Markdown lint.

Additional controlled 512-token tests on the same dependency versions reproduced
the default unpatched failure and passed exact CPU reload/recompute checks with
both explicit `BLHNC` on the base and the patched default. Every offload case
reloaded 83,226,624 bytes and reused 1,024 prompt tokens with FULL/PIECEWISE graphs.
The patched default matched both no-offload controls in the first matrix.
Repeats confirmed exact within-process reloads, but cold generation also varied
between independent unpatched no-offload launches. Both strict cross-process
matrices therefore remain failed; this is not a claim of full cross-launch
bitwise reproducibility. GPU resources were released after every case.

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" uv run --no-project --with pytest --with tblib python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py \
  tests/platforms/test_interface.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py -q --tb=short

uvx pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading_connector.py \
  tests/platforms/test_interface.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py \
  docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md
```

The model smoke used NVFP4 weights, a metadata-only 3-FP8/3-NVFP4 layer-wise KV
recipe, TP4 multiprocessing, FlashInfer attention, CUTLASS MoE, P64, prefix
caching, a 4,096-token context limit, 512 MiB GPU KV per rank, and a 4 GiB CPU
offload budget. It validates cache transparency, not benchmark accuracy.

## Scope and Related Work

This validates the built-in CPU tier on a fixed model/recipe/topology. It does
not certify NIXL P/D, LMCache, secondary tiers, or cross-topology canonical
offloading. Packed offloading still copies the complete backing row, including
unused space.

Duplicate-work checks covered RFC comments and open PR searches on September 29:
#53544 optimizes canonical-map derivation, #56953 compacts per-group CPU slots,
and #57216 fixes hybrid partial-tail scheduling. None changes this layout
negotiation; those changes are not duplicated here. #57824 improves the error
for mixed token-sized offload chunks; it does not change layout negotiation.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and this
description. This draft awaits submitting-author review before being marked
ready.

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

records.title: [KV Cache] Map kernel blocks per attention group; GLM-5.3-Flash on the generic packed layout
records.body:
## Purpose

Alternative to #57169 (and its earlier version #55219). It keeps #57169's GLM-5.3-Flash move to the generic packed KV layout with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail. It replaces the builder-side re-paging of the kpool indexer with a generic, worker-side kernel-block mapping per attention group. As a result, `BlockTable` / `BlockTables` stop knowing about kernel blocks.

**Design**
- **Block tables and slot mappings** are always in KV cache manager blocks, in V1 and MRv2. `kernel_block_sizes` is removed from `BlockTable`, `MultiGroupBlockTable`, `BlockTables`, both input batches and both slot-mapping kernels. Slot values are unchanged: `b*bs + off == (b*bpk + off//kbs)*kbs + off%kbs`.
- **Mapping per attention group.** When a group's backend needs blocks smaller than the manager's (`AttentionGroup.kernel_block_size`), `AttentionGroup.build_metadata` / `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` / `build_metadata_for_drafting` map its block table to kernel blocks. Kernel block `j` of block `b` is `b * kernel_block_stride + j`. The mapped table goes into a persistent per-ubatch buffer (`kernel_block_table`), so CUDA graphs see a stable address.
- **Ordinary splits.** In a dense (unpacked) layout the stride is blocks-per-kernel-block. KV views are allocated in kernel blocks as before.
- **Packed compressed caches.** Example: GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer, which DeepGEMM paged MQA reads in 32/64-state pages. `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache` re-strides the bound view over the packed blocks and takes the stride from the real tensor. It raises for token caches, which are written through manager-unit slot mappings.
- **Alignment.** A backend with only fixed kernel block sizes gets `block_stride_alignment = MultipleOf(max size)` (`customize_attention_spec`). `KVCacheSpec.get_block_stride_alignment()` resolves it in the engine against the *final* (possibly rescaled) block size, and returns 1 when the block runs whole.
- **Connectors** keep manager-block views. NIXL and Mooncake inline the removed `BlockTable.map_to_kernel_blocks`.

**Related:**
- #58630 resolves kernel block-size constraints per spec.
- #59112 re-pages packed BLHNC caches inside FlashInfer.

This PR instead makes kernel blocks a per-attention-group concern in the worker.

## Test Plan / Results

Run on B300 with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`, one file at a time. Running several of these files in one process fails the same way on the base branch, from cross-file interference.

- **Unit tests, passing:**
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`, including new tests for packed and split mapping, the token-cache error, and `MultipleOf` alignment resolution;
  - `test_gpu_block_table.py`, `test_gpu_input_batch.py`, `test_gpu_model_runner.py`, `test_kv_block_zeroer.py`, `test_gpu_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`, `test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`;
  - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py`, `test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py`;
  - `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (129);
  - `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py` (42), `test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`;
  - `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` (152 on its own);
  - `tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py`;
  - `tests/models/glm5next`.
- **Unit tests, known failure:** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_length.py::test_eagle3_acceptance_length[FLASH_ATTN-...-gpt-oss-20b-eagle3]` fails on this branch (0.483) and on the reference branch (0.486) against a 0.4864 minimum, so it's pre-existing on this machine.
- **End-to-end greedy equivalence.** The reference is the same tree without the generic block-table change, which matches `main` for non-GLM models. FlashInfer autotuning was off and MoE was Triton, for determinism.
  - **GLM-5.3-Flash, dummy weights, packed indexer mapping:** bitwise identical tokens and top-5 logprobs for V2 CUDA graphs at block 1024, V1 CUDA graphs at block 1024, V2 with MTP 3 at block 1024, and V2 eager at block 256.
  - **GLM-4.7-Flash with MTP, `FLASHINFER_MLA`, block 256 split into 64 (V1):** bitwise identical, and reruns are stable.
  - **Qwen3-8B with EAGLE3, `FLASHINFER` in the HND `LBHNC` layout, block 256 split into 64 (V1):** bitwise identical.
  - **V2 runner with MTP on GLM-4.7-Flash:** not deterministic run to run, even on the reference branch, so it's not comparable.
- **Not yet run:** accuracy evals on real GLM-5.3-Flash weights.

## AI assistance

records.title: [MoE] Select DeepEP v2 dispatch layout per forward
records.body:
## Purpose

DeepEP v2 currently selects one dispatch layout from `enforce_eager` when the MoE layer is initialized. A server with CUDA graphs enabled therefore uses the contiguous, worst-case allocation layout even for forwards that execute eagerly.

Select the layout from the current forward's `cudagraph_runtime_mode`: `NONE` uses expanded dispatch with CPU counts and exact allocation; `FULL` and `PIECEWISE` use contiguous dispatch without CPU synchronization. Preserve that choice in the deferred receiver so its expert metadata matches the dispatch even if the forward context changes.

The backend correctness test switches the same instance between eager and graph modes and captures/replays a full CUDA graph before returning to eager execution.

### Duplicate-work checks

Open PR searches covered `DeepEP v2`, `deepep_v2 do_expand`, `deepep cudagraph runtime`, and `51166 in:body`. #51166 changes the initialization-time gate from `enforce_eager` to the configured graph mode; this change instead selects the layout for each forward and preserves the choice through asynchronous receive. #51589 adds an opt-in token threshold for expanded sync-less prefill and reconstructs metadata on the GPU; this change retains the existing synchronized expanded layout for eager forwards. #50511 addresses padding and metadata correctness, without runtime mode selection.

## Test Plan

Run the CPU prepare/finalize contracts, two-GPU BF16/FP8 reference comparisons, full CUDA graph capture/replay and mode transitions, and GSM8K using eager prefill with graph decode on two Pirate B200 GPUs.

## Test Result

- All pre-commit hooks passed on the changed files, including sign-off checks on both commits.
- Local isolated CPU contracts: 4 passed.
- Pirate CPU contracts with real vLLM/DeepEP imports: 4 passed.
- Pirate two-B200 GPU suite: 17 passed in 275.73s, with no skips. Both ranks passed an explicit NCCL GIN type 2 preflight with device-plugin allocated RDMA devices. Coverage includes BF16/FP8 reference comparisons, transitions on the same instance (`NONE → FULL → PIECEWISE → NONE`), and full CUDA graph capture/replay for three expert backends.
- GSM8K: 1 passed; **89.84% accuracy**, 1,319 questions, five-shot, zero invalid answers. Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block`, DP=2, EP enabled, `deepep_v2`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (eager prefill and graph decode). Configured threshold 0.85 with the suite's default tolerance 0.08; measured accuracy exceeds 0.85.
- The Kueue validation Job completed successfully (exit 0). Temporary RDMA queue quota was restored to its original configuration.

Commands run in separate pytest processes:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_async_finalize.py -vv -s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py -vv -s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=/results/deepep-dynamic-pirate-20260929-r5/gsm8k-list.txt -vv -s
```

GSM8K server arguments:

```text
--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048
--data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_v2
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.7
--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Artifacts are retained under `/results/deepep-dynamic-pirate-20260929-r5` on the Pirate `tms-shared-cache` PVC. Validation used two GPUs on one B200 node; this does not establish cross-node coverage or a performance improvement.

Validation source: `194a32c9952278d9129c3c5d044d2f86d4aa2bae`. Runtime image: `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:0ad6fa4178c34f4e04402452bbc4294df6dd2fb2785a0ecd402b2861aea2a189`, with its Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and NCCL 2.30.7 stack retained and the Python source installed editable.

### AI assistance

AI assistance was used to implement the change, extend the tests, run validation, and prepare this description. This is a draft: before marking it ready, the human submitter must review every changed line, run relevant tests and model validation, and understand and be able to defend the change end to end.

records.title: [Attention][MLA] Support nvfp4_ds_mla on FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE, with native NVFP4 decode
records.body:
## Purpose

`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` (the TRTLLM-gen sparse MLA backend on SM10x) now accepts `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`, which only `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` accepted. The NVFP4 cache holds 1.6x the tokens of an FP8 one (352 vs 576 bytes per token).

Three commits:

1. **FP8 staging**, based on Chi McIsaac's work (`Co-authored-by` in the commit). The TRTLLM-gen kernel reads FP8 rows only, so each layer stages the rows it attends to as FP8 (`dequant / k_scale`): decode and spec-decode tokens gather their top-k rows, prefill tokens share one context gather per request and chunk (Triton kernels in `nvfp4_ds_mla_fp8_gather.py`). The staging workspace is reserved up front so the memory profile accounts for it. The dtype needs `kv_lora_rank` 512 and `qk_rope_head_dim` 64 and is rejected with context parallelism and with HiSparse. The backend reports `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA-graph support for it, because the prefill gather is planned on the host. The impl and builder get class-level defaults for the new attributes, because existing tests build them with `object.__new__`, and `get_cudagraph_support` accepts the `None` config that one existing test passes.
2. **Native decode.** When FlashInfer provides `flashinfer.mla.nvfp4_sparse_mla_decode` (experimental; FlashInfer PR https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5717), the layer has 16 heads per rank, the top-k width is 512, 1024 or 2048 and the GPU is SM100 or SM103, decode reads the cache rows as stored: no staging copy, no decode staging workspace, and no e4m3 re-rounding of the dequantized values. Both fp8 bmm scales are divided by `k_scale`, because the staged rows they were built for hold `dequant / k_scale` while the native kernel reads exact values. Everything else keeps the staged path, and this commit does nothing until a FlashInfer release contains the op (`has_flashinfer_nvfp4_sparse_mla_decode()`).
3. **Tests.** `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness` already parametrizes `nvfp4_ds_mla` and skipped it for this backend. Once the backend accepts the dtype those cases run, and they failed: the mock layer quantized the query to fp8 only for `fp8*` caches, while `MLAAttention` does it for every quantized cache. The mock now does the same, and the FlashInfer `nvfp4_ds_mla` cases use the fp8 tolerance (the backend reads them with an fp8 query and staged fp8 rows).

**Backend selection is unchanged** (part of the first commit). On SM10x, auto-selection prefers `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` for every quantized KV dtype, so accepting `nvfp4_ds_mla` would have moved existing users of that dtype from `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` to the staged path without a benchmark. `nvfp4_ds_mla` keeps `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` first and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` as the fallback; this path is opt-in with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, and `test_sm100_quantized_sparse_priority` pins the order. Making it the default needs numbers against FlashMLA's NVFP4 kernels, which this PR does not have.

**Not a duplicate.** Checks run as `AGENTS.md` prescribes, 2026-09-29: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` with `"nvfp4_ds_mla"`, `"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE"`, `"nvfp4 flashinfer sparse mla"` and `"FlashInfer nvfp4 decode MLA"`. No open PR adds `nvfp4_ds_mla` to `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, and `flashinfer_mla_sparse.py` on `main` has no NVFP4 support. Related, separate: #58744 (mine; touches `mla_attention.py`'s chunked-context gather, not this backend) and #53770 (a `fp8_k_nvfp4_v` KV format for the non-MLA FlashInfer backend).

**AI assistance:** this PR was prepared with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5); the commits carry `Co-Authored-By` trailers.

## Test Plan

Hardware: one B300 SXM6 (SM103, driver 580.173.02), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer at PR https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5717.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_nvfp4_native_decode.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py
```

The first file is new. `test_native_decode_matches_staged_decode` runs FlashInfer's native decode and the FP8-staged decode over a per-layer cache whose blocks alternate with another layer's, with `k_scale` 1 and 0.5, and checks both against an exact FP32 reference (native under 1 %, staged under 6 %, native vs staged under 6 %). `test_backend_native_decode_folds_k_scale` calls the backend's own `_nvfp4_decode` (impl built without `__init__` and the index conversion stubbed, as the neighbouring tests do) and checks it against the same reference with `k_scale` 1 and 0.5, so a missing `1 / k_scale` on either bmm scale fails it.

## Test Result

B300 SXM6 (SM103), PR head `0e2b2810e8` against upstream `main` `4e0a414c44`:

| Selection | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_nvfp4_native_decode.py` (new) | n/a | 10 passed |
| `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` | 396 passed, 378 skipped | 480 passed, 294 skipped |
| `test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`, `test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_workspace.py` | 46 passed | 46 passed |
| 7 other files that mention the backend | 206 passed, 27 skipped | 212 passed, 27 skipped |

The 84 extra passes in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` are the FlashInfer x `nvfp4_ds_mla` cases of `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness`, which the backend used to skip. The 6 extra passes in the other files are the new `test_sm100_quantized_sparse_priority` cases. The 7 other files are `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py`, `test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py`, `test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py`, `test_cuda_backend_probe_errors.py`, `test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py` and `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py`. `test_mla_backends.py` (335 dense-MLA tests) was not run to completion; none of its tests reach code this PR changes.

GSM8K, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 20-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, GLM-5.3 with NVFP4 weights, TP4 on four B300 GPUs, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, no speculative decoding:

| `--kv-cache-dtype` | accuracy | 95 % interval | invalid responses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fp8` | 89.69 % (1183/1319) | 87.9 to 91.2 % | 0 |
| `nvfp4_ds_mla` | 89.76 % (1184/1319) | 88.0 to 91.3 % | 1 |

The NVFP4 server logged that decode used FlashInfer's native kernel. The 20-shot prompts are 3,545 to 3,708 tokens, above the 2,048 top-k, so prefill took the staged sparse path. At the same memory budget the KV cache held 4,526,592 tokens with `nvfp4_ds_mla` and 2,870,464 with `fp8` (1.58x). One run per arm, each server on a different node. The servers ran an earlier revision of this branch, before the class-level defaults, the `None` guard, the selection-order change and two tests. The eval names `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` explicitly, and none of those changes alters an instance built through `__init__`.

Limits of the evidence:

- The FlashInfer-backend `nvfp4_ds_mla` cases in `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness` use 128 total heads at TP 1, 2 and 4 and top-k 128, so they run the staged path end to end. The native branch is covered by the backend-level test above (top-k index conversion stubbed) and by the GSM8K run (16 heads per rank at TP4).
- GSM8K shows no accuracy loss on this task. It does not cover long-context retrieval or tool calls, and speculative decoding was off.

records.title: [Perf][KV Connector] Drop the redundant index_select in kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive
records.body:
## Purpose

`kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive` rewrites the blocks that were just copied
into the local cache so that their layout matches what the local attention
backend expects. It gathers them, permutes the two inner dimensions and writes
them back:

```python
blocks_to_update = cache.index_select(0, indices)      # line 283
target_shape = list(blocks_to_update.shape)
target_shape[0] = -1
inv_order = [0, 1, 3, 2, 4] if blocks_to_update.ndim == 5 else [0, 2, 1, 3]
src_shape = tuple(target_shape[i] for i in inv_order)
blocks_to_update = cache.index_select(0, indices)      # line 288 - identical
permuted_blocks = blocks_to_update.reshape(src_shape).permute(*inv_order)
cache.index_copy_(0, indices, permuted_blocks)
```

Line 288 repeats line 283 verbatim and immediately overwrites its result with
an identical tensor, so the reshape/permute/copy are unaffected by it. The
first call is needed (`target_shape`/`inv_order` are derived from its shape and
ndim); the second is not.

`index_select` is a full gather of every received block, and this runs on the
decode side for each received block set, so the duplicate doubles a temporary
allocation proportional to the transferred KV. Deleting the statement is
behaviour-preserving; the only observable difference is one fewer gather.

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py` wraps a
real `torch` cache tensor so the gathers and the write-back are counted, and
runs the helper for both the 4D and the 5D cache layout:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py -q
```

Besides the call counts it also pins the operation's contract - a layout fix-up
is a permutation, so the received blocks must keep their multiset of values and
untouched blocks must be left alone - which guards against a future change that
"optimises" the remaining gather away or reorders the permutation.

## Test Result

```
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py ..   [100%]
2 passed
```

On the unpatched tree the same test reports two gathers and fails:

```
FAILED .../test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py::test_the_received_blocks_are_gathered_once[4d_cache]
FAILED .../test_kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive.py::test_the_received_blocks_are_gathered_once[5d_cache]
2 failed
```

Tested on main (`105a4e09`), Linux x86_64 / Python 3.12, CPU-only `torch`.
